findings.evidence: Artin.lean:355-360 (`(indVirtualCharactersAddHom ... (fun C ↦ IsCyclic C)).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ`); the only cyclic input to the proof is `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic f.2` at line 392. `grep -rn cyclicInductionRatLinearMap TauCeti` shows no in-repo consumer.
findings.fix: Parameterize on `P`: `indVirtualCharactersRatLinearMap (P : Subgroup G → Prop)` with the corresponding `_tmul` simp lemma, and a general surjectivity lemma taking the hypothesis `(n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : ∀ f ∈ virtualCharacters k G, n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P)`. Then `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap_surjective` is `P := IsCyclic, n := Nat.card G`, and the elementary case is one line from `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isElementary`.
findings.issue: `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap` and its `@[simp]` lemma `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap_tmul` are defined only for `fun C ↦ IsCyclic C`, although the definition is literally `(indVirtualCharactersAddHom P).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ` for `P := IsCyclic` and neither the definition nor the `_tmul` proof (lines 365-372) mentions cyclicity. `indVirtualCharactersAddHom` was deliberately built for an arbitrary `P` (Ideal.lean:142); the base change should be too. The surjectivity proof (lines 379-407) likewise only uses `∃ n ≠ 0, ∀ f ∈ virtualCharacters k G, n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`, so as stated it cannot be reused for the elementary family whose sharp membership this same file proves (line 579).

findings.evidence: Sharp theorem at Artin.lean:344; `indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic` at Artin.lean:558 identifies the target with the span of the induced irreducible characters. The family is finite: this PR's `cyclicSubgroupFintype` (Artin.lean:99) plus `finEquivIrreducibleCharacters`/`irreducibleRepresentation` (CharacterTable/Table.lean:181-197), and `ind` depends only on the character (used at Artin.lean:544-549).
findings.fix: State the finite-family theorem with the multiplier `Nat.card G` and derive it from `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` plus `indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic`, taking the fixed family to be `irreducibleRepresentation k i` over the finitely many cyclic subgroups; drop the determinant machinery (or keep it only if an index/determinant statement is actually made, which the roadmap treats as a separate target).
findings.issue: `exists_sum_zsmul_ind_ofCharacter_eq_zsmul_cyclic` still asserts only `∃ d ≠ 0`, obtained by the ~120-line determinant/lattice-descent route (`sum_adjugate_smul_eq_det_smul`, `det_ne_zero_of_span_eq_top`, `exists_zsmul_mem_span_int`, `exists_artin_induction_data`). Under its own hypotheses `[IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]` the same statement holds with `d = Nat.card G`, so the PR exports a weaker multiplier alongside the sharp one it proves, and the whole descent apparatus is a weaker duplicate of the general result.

summary: The sharp Artin statements are at the right level, but the rationalized induction map is needlessly specialized to the cyclic family (its definition and `_tmul` lemma use nothing about cyclicity, and the surjectivity argument only needs a nonzero multiplier), and the retained determinant development proves an unspecified `d` where the sharp theorem now gives `|G|` for the same fixed family.
